title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction from Plant Nuclei for Long-Read Sequencing
author: Cedric Mariac
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.83shyne

steps.title: Sample and grind plant tissue
steps.instruction: Collect 0.7–1 g of fresh plant tissue into a 50 mL tube pre‑filled with liquid nitrogen, then grind the frozen tissue in a mortar stored at –80 °C using a pestle, avoiding mixing tissues of different developmental stages.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue and filter nuclei
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen powder into an ice‑cold 50 mL tube containing 25 mL ice‑cold WB, filter the homogenate through a single layer of Scrynel polyester filter (25 µm mesh) into an ice‑cold 50 mL centrifuge bottle, squeeze the remaining homogenate with gloved hands to recover nuclei, and lyse the filtrate by passing it through a DOUNCE first with a loose fitting (A) ten times, then with a tighter fitting (B) ten times.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei and wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 2 500 × g, 4 °C for 20 min (adjust time for species) using a fixed‑angle rotor; discard supernatant, add 1 mL ice‑cold WB and gently resuspend the pellet (a small paint brush may be used), then bring the volume up to 25 mL with ice‑cold WB and centrifuge again at 2 500 × g, 4 °C for 15 min in a swinging‑bucket rotor; discard supernatant and resuspend the nuclei pellet in 5 mL MATAB lysis buffer supplemented with 17 µL spermine, 17 µL spermidine, and 20 µL DTT.

steps.title: Lyse nuclei and extract DNA
steps.instruction: Incubate the nuclei suspension at 65 °C for 1 h, mixing once with extreme precaution; add 10 µL proteinase K (20 mg mL⁻¹, e.g., Terra PCR Kit, Clonectec) and incubate at 55 °C for 1 h 45 min; gently pour the mixture into a 15 mL tube, add 5 mL 24:1 chloroform/isoamyl alcohol, agitate horizontally at 5 rpm for 10 min, then centrifuge 20 min at 5 500 × g, 15 °C; transfer the supernatant to a clean 15 mL tube, add 10 µL RNase A (Promega, 1 mg mL⁻¹), mix by inversion and incubate 30 min at room temperature; add another 5 mL 24:1 chloroform/isoamyl alcohol, agitate at 5 rpm for 10 min under a chemical hood, centrifuge 20 min at 5 500 × g, 15 °C, and transfer the supernatant to a clean tube. Perform a total of 2–3 chloroform extractions; if the second extraction yields a clear phase, the third may be omitted.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of 3 M sodium acetate and 4 mL isopropanol (room temperature) to the cleared lysate, agitate horizontally at 5 rpm until a medusa‑like DNA precipitate forms; collect the DNA with a glass hook and transfer it first into a 10 mL tube containing 70 % ethanol, then into a 2 mL tube with 2 mL 70 % ethanol; centrifuge 10 min at 10 000 × g, discard the supernatant, dry the pellet at 45 °C for 15 min, and finally resuspend in 100 µL sterile H₂O.

steps.title: Clean up DNA with AMPure
steps.instruction: Purify the DNA using AMPure beads at a 1 × vol/vol ratio, then perform two washes with 70 % ethanol; resuspend the cleaned DNA in 50 µL DNAse‑free water and adjust the final volume to obtain a concentration of 300–400 ng µL⁻¹.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer and a Qubit fluorometer, ensuring the NanoDrop/Qubit ratio is less than 2.

steps.title: Assess DNA size by PFGE
steps.instruction: Load 20 µL of DNA (containing 1.5–5.5 µg DNA) mixed with 5 µL 6× loading buffer onto a 1 % agarose gel and run pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis using the following parameters: pulse time initial = 5 s, final = 117 s; run time = 20.5 h; voltage = 5 V cm⁻¹; angle = 120°; temperature = 14 °C; end‑of‑run current = 255 mA.
